content.key_idea: A typical cloud object storage service (COSS) exposes only a constrained RESTful API through a shared, stateless proxy layer, behind which a separate metadata service and data service are strictly isolated from applications.
content.reading_order: Top-down: several applications share one Cloud SDK, crossing a RESTful-API boundary into a stateless Proxy Layer (Proxy 1..n), which talks to a separate Metadata Service and Data Service inside the Object Storage Service.

summary: Mantle is a hierarchical metadata management system for cloud object storage services (COSS) that replaces a monolithic metadata service with a scalable sharded database (TafDB) plus a per-namespace index (IndexNode). Figure 1 instead sets up the background: the architecture of a typical existing COSS. Multiple applications (Data Warehouse, AI Training, ...) sit above a shared Cloud SDK, crossing a dashed RESTful-API (HTTP GET/PUT) boundary into the cloud service. Inside the Object Storage Service, a stateless Proxy Layer of interchangeable proxies (Proxy 1...Proxy n) receives every request and talks bidirectionally to a separate Metadata Service, which resolves object paths, and a Data Service, which stores the object bytes. This three-component, proxy-fronted split is the baseline architecture that Mantle's own proxy layer continues to follow, even as Mantle changes what sits behind it.
